channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Making MLLMs Blind: Adversarial Smuggling Attacks in MLLM Content Moderation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces “Adversarial Smuggling Attacks” against multimodal LLM (MLLM) content moderation, hiding harmful content in human-readable visual formats that models can’t reliably parse.
  • Defines two attack pathways: Perceptual Blindness (disrupt text recognition) and Reasoning Blockade (block semantic understanding even when OCR succeeds).
  • Builds SmuggleBench with 1,700 attack instances and shows high vulnerability (ASR > 90%) across proprietary and open-source models.
  • Explores preliminary mitigations including test-time scaling (CoT) and adversarial training (SFT).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zhiheng Li', 'Zongyang Ma', 'Yuntong Pan', 'Ziqi Zhang', 'Xiaolei Lv', 'Bo Li', 'Jun Gao', 'Jianing Zhang', 'Chunfeng Yuan', 'Bing Li', 'Weiming Hu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-attacks', 'multimodal-llms', 'content-moderation-evasion', 'adversarial-smuggling', 'benchmark']

item.title: Adversarial Evasion Attacks on Computer Vision using SHAP Values
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a white-box adversarial evasion attack for computer vision models that uses SHAP values to identify influential input features at inference time.
  • Shows that the attack can reduce model output confidence and cause misclassifications with perturbations intended to remain imperceptible to humans.
  • Compares the SHAP-based attack against FGSM and reports stronger misclassification generation, especially under gradient-hiding conditions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Frank Mollard', 'Marcus Becker', 'Florian Roehrbein']
  • Tags: ['adversarial evasion', 'computer vision', 'SHAP interpretability', 'white-box attacks', 'gradient masking/gradient hiding']

item.title: RDSplat: Robust Watermarking for 3D Gaussian Splatting Against 2D and 3D Diffusion Editing
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes RDSplat, a robust watermarking framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) that resists diffusion-based editing.
  • Embeds 100-bit watermarks into low-frequency primitives selected via Frequency-Aware Primitive Selection (FAPS) and freezes higher-frequency primitives.
  • Introduces GeoMark decoder (ViT-based) with spatially periodic secret embedding to recover watermarks under both 2D and 3D diffusion edits.
  • Evaluates against multiple 2D diffusion attacks and iterative 3D editing, reporting strong bit accuracy and fast fine-tuning.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Longjie Zhao', 'Ziming Hong', 'Zhenyang Ren', 'Runnan Chen', 'Mingming Gong', 'Tongliang Liu']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'watermarking', 'adversarial/diffusion attacks', '3D generative editing', 'robustness']

item.title: Nearest Neighbor Projection Removal Adversarial Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an adversarial training method that improves robustness by mitigating inter-class feature overlap.
  • For each adversarial sample, it identifies nearest inter-class neighbors in feature space and projects out (removes) their influence.
  • Includes theoretical analysis via logits correction to reduce Lipschitz constant and Rademacher complexity.
  • Evaluates on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, and TinyImagenet with results competitive with strong adversarial training baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Himanshu Singh', 'A. V. Subramanyam', 'Shivank Rajput', 'Mohan Kankanhalli']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-training', 'adversarial-examples', 'feature-space-projection', 'robustness', 'nearest-neighbor-interclass']

item.title: Privacy Attacks on Image AutoRegressive Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents a comprehensive privacy/security analysis of image autoregressive (IAR) models.
  • Introduces a novel membership inference attack (MIA) that reliably detects whether training images were used.
  • Uses the MIA to perform dataset inference and training data extraction, recovering hundreds of training datapoints from an IAR.
  • Finds IARs exhibit significantly higher privacy leakage than diffusion models under comparable attack settings.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Antoni Kowalczuk', "Jan Dubi\\'nski", 'Franziska Boenisch', 'Adam Dziedzic']
  • Tags: ['privacy attacks', 'membership inference', 'dataset inference', 'training data extraction', 'image generative models']

item.title: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Semantic-level UI Element Injection as a practical red-teaming threat against GUI agents by overlaying injected UI elements onto screenshots to misdirect visual grounding.
  • Uses an Editor-Overlapper-Victim pipeline with iterative optimization and prompt adaptation to maximize attack success across multiple victim models.
  • Finds up to 4.4x improvement over random injection and strong cross-model transferability of optimized attacks.
  • Shows injected elements can act as persistent attractors, leading to repeated agent clicks after initial success.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenkui Yang', 'Chao Jin', 'Haisu Zhu', 'Weilin Luo', 'Derek Yuen', 'Kun Shao', 'Huaibo Huang', 'Junxian Duan', 'Jie Cao', 'Ran He']
  • Tags: ['GUI Agents', 'Semantic UI Injection', 'Red Teaming', 'Visual Prompting/Overlay Attacks', 'Adversarial Attacks']

item.title: SyncBreaker:Stage-Aware Multimodal Adversarial Attacks on Audio-Driven Talking Head Generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SyncBreaker, a stage-aware multimodal framework to thwart audio-driven talking-head generation by jointly perturbing portrait (image) and audio inputs.
  • Introduces Multi-Interval Sampling–based nullifying supervision to steer diffusion outputs toward a static reference portrait across denoising stages.
  • Introduces Cross-Attention Fooling to suppress interval-specific audio-conditioned cross-attention responses, degrading lip-sync and facial dynamics.
  • Evaluates in a white-box proactive protection setting and reports improved attack effectiveness over single-modality baselines while maintaining perceptual quality and robustness to purification.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenli Zhang', 'Xianglong Shi', 'Sirui Zhao', 'Xinqi Chen', 'Guo Cheng', 'Yifan Xu', 'Tong Xu', 'Yong Liao']
  • Tags: ['Multimodal adversarial attacks', 'Audio-driven generation', 'Diffusion-stage attacks', 'Lip-sync degradation', 'Adversarial robustness/proactive protection']

item.title: Phantasia: Context-Adaptive Backdoors in Vision Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Phantasia, a context-adaptive backdoor attack for Vision-Language Models that generates contextually coherent yet malicious responses.
  • Shows prior VLM backdoor attack stealth is overestimated and demonstrates that cross-domain defense techniques can detect them effectively.
  • Reports extensive experiments across multiple VLM architectures with improved attack success rates while preserving benign behavior under defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Nam Duong Tran', 'Phi Le Nguyen']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'vision-language models (VLMs)', 'context-adaptive poisoning', 'attack stealth/evasion', 'defense evaluation']

item.title: $\oslash$ Source Models Leak What They Shouldn't $\nrightarrow$: Unlearning Zero-Shot Transfer in Domain Adaptation Through Adversarial Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies privacy leakage of source-domain information through domain adaptation in vision models.
  • Proposes a machine unlearning approach (SCADA-UL) to unlearn source-exclusive classes via adversarial optimization.
  • Introduces/extends unlearning settings for distribution shift and unknown/continual forget-class scenarios.
  • Evaluates against existing machine unlearning baselines, reporting retraining-level unlearning performance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Arnav Devalapally', 'Poornima Jain', 'Kartik Srinivas', 'Vineeth N. Balasubramanian']
  • Tags: ['machine unlearning', 'privacy leakage', 'domain adaptation', 'adversarial optimization', 'source data protection']

item.title: SciFigDetect: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Scientific Figure Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SciFigDetect, a benchmark specifically for detecting AI-generated scientific figures (a visual forensics/research integrity setting distinct from generic AIGI detection).
  • Constructs a dataset using an agent-based pipeline that generates candidate figures from scientific papers and refines/filters them via a review loop, including aligned real–synthetic pairs.
  • Evaluates multiple detectors across zero-shot, cross-generator, and degraded-image/post-processing conditions, finding poor transfer, generator overfitting, and fragility under corruptions.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['You Hu', 'Chenzhuo Zhao', 'Changfa Mo', 'Haotian Liu', 'Xiaobai Li']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'visual forensics', 'benchmarking', 'robustness to post-processing', 'research integrity']

item.title: FlowGuard: Towards Lightweight In-Generation Safety Detection for Diffusion Models via Linear Latent Decoding
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes FlowGuard, a lightweight in-generation safety detection method for diffusion models that operates on intermediate denoising steps.
  • Targets early detection of NSFW content during latent diffusion to bridge the gap between prompt-level safety and final-image safety.
  • Uses linear latent decoding approximation plus curriculum learning to enable detection despite noisy intermediate latents.
  • Evaluates on a cross-model benchmark (nine diffusion backbones) and reports improved F1 and substantial efficiency/memory reductions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jinghan Yang', 'Yihe Fan', 'Xudong Pan', 'Min Yang']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'In-generation detection', 'Diffusion models', 'NSFW filtering', 'Latent diffusion']

item.title: Beyond Surface Artifacts: Capturing Shared Latent Forgery Knowledge Across Modalities
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a modality-agnostic forgery (MAF) detection framework to improve multimodal deepfake forensics generalization beyond superficial artifacts.
  • Introduces benchmark DeepModal-Bench to evaluate generalization across unseen or “dark” modalities using weak (correlated) and strong (isolated) settings.
  • Focuses on extracting shared latent forgery knowledge by decoupling modality-specific styles, aiming for robust detection across modalities.
  • Positions the work as a universal defense mechanism for multimodal forgery detection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jingtong Dou', 'Chuancheng Shi', 'Jian Wang', 'Fei Shen', 'Zhiyong Wang', 'Tat-Seng Chua']
  • Tags: ['multimodal-forensics', 'deepfake-detection', 'adversarial-robustness', 'defense-generalization', 'benchmarking']

item.title: Auditing Black-Box LLM APIs with a Rank-Based Uniformity Test
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a rank-based statistical test to audit black-box LLM APIs by checking behavioral equality with an authentic local model.
  • Designed to be query-efficient and robust against adversarial providers that detect or reroute testing attempts.
  • Evaluates detection across threat scenarios including quantization, harmful fine-tuning, jailbreak prompting, and full model substitution.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xiaoyuan Zhu', 'Yaowen Ye', 'Tianyi Qiu', 'Hanlin Zhu', 'Sijun Tan', 'Ajraf Mannan', 'Jonathan Michala', 'Raluca Ada Popa', 'Willie Neiswanger']
  • Tags: ['LLM security auditing', 'Black-box evaluation', 'Model substitution detection', 'Robust statistical testing', 'Safety/jailbreak threats']

item.title: Break Me If You Can: Self-Jailbreaking of Aligned LLMs via Lexical Insertion Prompting
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces a new threat model called self-jailbreaking where the target aligned LLM helps guide its own compromise without external red-team tools.
  • Proposes SLIP (Self-Jailbreaking via Lexical Insertion Prompting), a black-box breadth-first search approach that incrementally inserts goal-related missing content words into benign prompts using the target model as the guide.
  • Evaluates SLIP on AdvBench and HarmBench, reporting 90–100% attack success rates across many models with relatively few model calls.
  • Assesses existing defenses and proposes the Semantic Drift Monitor (SDM) defense, achieving 76% detection at 5% FPR, while noting adaptive attacks can still bypass it.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Devang Kulshreshtha', 'Hang Su', 'Haibo Jin', 'Chinmay Hegde', 'Haohan Wang']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'prompt injection-style attacks', 'self-jailbreaking', 'adversarial evaluation', 'defense detection']

item.title: Hallucination Detection and Evaluation of Large Language Model
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes HHEM, a lightweight, classification-based hallucination detection/evaluation framework for LLMs that avoids relying on additional LLM verification steps.
  • Compares hallucination detection performance across multiple LLMs using QA and summarization tasks, reporting metrics like TPR, TNR, and accuracy; notes major reduction in evaluation time (8 hours to ~10 minutes).
  • Introduces segment-based retrieval to better detect localized hallucinations in summarization by verifying smaller text components.
  • Finds model-size-dependent trends in hallucination frequency/instability via CDF analysis and evaluates enhancements like non-fabrication checking.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chenggong Zhang', 'Haopeng Wang', 'Hexi Meng']
  • Tags: ['hallucination-detection', 'LLM-evaluation', 'factuality-verification', 'robustness', 'lightweight-classification']

item.title: PIArena: A Platform for Prompt Injection Evaluation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces PIArena, a unified platform to evaluate prompt injection attacks and defenses consistently across benchmarks and tasks.
  • Includes an adaptive, strategy-based attack that optimizes injected prompts using defense feedback.
  • Empirically shows limitations of existing defenses, including poor cross-task generalization and vulnerability to adaptive attacks, especially when injected tasks align with the target task.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Runpeng Geng', 'Chenlong Yin', 'Yanting Wang', 'Ying Chen', 'Jinyuan Jia']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection', 'adversarial evaluation', 'AI security', 'attack-defense benchmarking', 'robustness/generalization']

item.title: ACIArena: Toward Unified Evaluation for Agent Cascading Injection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ACIArena, a unified evaluation framework for Multi-Agent Systems under Agent Cascading Injection (ACI) attacks.
  • Covers multiple attack surfaces (external inputs, agent profiles, inter-agent messages) and attack objectives (instruction hijacking, task disruption, information exfiltration).
  • Provides a benchmark of 1,356 test cases across six MAS implementations and includes attack-defense module support.
  • Findings indicate that topology-only evaluation is insufficient and that defenses from simplified settings may not transfer and can introduce new vulnerabilities.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hengyu An', 'Minxi Li', 'Jinghuai Zhang', 'Naen Xu', 'Chunyi Zhou', 'Changjiang Li', 'Xiaogang Xu', 'Tianyu Du', 'Shouling Ji']
  • Tags: ['agent cascading injection', 'multi-agent system security', 'red teaming/robustness evaluation', 'attack surfaces & objectives', 'benchmarking']

item.title: The Art of (Mis)alignment: How Fine-Tuning Methods Effectively Misalign and Realign LLMs in Post-Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how fine-tuning methods (SFT and preference-based tuning like ORPO and DPO) can be used to induce misalignment in safety-aligned LLMs.
  • Investigates the possibility of “realignment” (restoring safety) via fine-tuning after misalignment.
  • Evaluates method-specific effectiveness, model-specific resistance, and effects of multi-round adversarial dynamics.
  • Emphasizes need for robust safeguards and customized safety alignment strategies against adversarial exploitation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rui Zhang', 'Hongwei Li', 'Yun Shen', 'Xinyue Shen', 'Wenbo Jiang', 'Guowen Xu', 'Yang Liu', 'Michael Backes', 'Yang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'misalignment attacks', 'fine-tuning attacks/defense', 'safety alignment', 'red-teaming/evaluation']

item.title: IatroBench: Pre-Registered Evidence of Iatrogenic Harm from AI Safety Measures
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces IatroBench, a pre-registered evaluation benchmark for measuring iatrogenic harm caused by AI safety measures in clinical guidance.
  • Compares model outputs across physician vs. layperson framing for multiple frontier LLMs, focusing on omission harm (withholding needed/appropriate guidance) and commission harm (unsafe/incorrect guidance).
  • Finds identity-contingent withholding: safety-colliding action hit rates decrease in layperson framing, but clinically appropriate guidance is also omitted for physician framing, especially in heavily safety-trained models.
  • Identifies distinct failure modes including trained withholding, incompetence, and indiscriminate content filtering that disproportionately removes physician-like answers.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking / Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['David Gringras']
  • Tags: ['AI safety evaluation', 'Omission/withholding harm', 'Prompt/framing sensitivity', 'Benchmarking/red-teaming', 'Clinical guidance risk']

item.title: Guardian-as-an-Advisor: Advancing Next-Generation Guardian Models for Trustworthy LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “Guardian-as-an-Advisor,” a soft-gating safety pipeline where a guardian model predicts risk labels/explanations and prepends advice to the user query for re-inference.
  • Introduces GuardSet (208k+ multi-domain dataset) with robustness and honesty-focused slices for training/evaluating safety detection and behavior.
  • Trains the guardian using SFT plus RL to enforce consistency between risk labels and explanations, aiming to reduce over-refusal while maintaining safety compliance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yue Huang', 'Haomin Zhuang', 'Jiayi Ye', 'Han Bao', 'Yanbo Wang', 'Hang Hua', 'Siyuan Wu', 'Pin-Yu Chen', 'Xiangliang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'attack detection', 'guardrails', 'adversarial robustness', 'honesty/consistency']

item.title: How Independent are Large Language Models? A Statistical Framework for Auditing Behavioral Entanglement and Reweighting Verifier Ensembles
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a statistical auditing framework to measure hidden behavioral entanglement and correlated failures among black-box LLMs.
  • Introduces two information-theoretic metrics (a Difficulty-Weighted Behavioral Entanglement Index and CIG) and studies their impact on LLM-as-a-judge evaluation reliability.
  • Shows entanglement correlates with degraded judge precision/over-endorsement bias across multiple LLM families.
  • Demonstrates a defense-like mitigation via entangled-verifier ensemble reweighting to reduce correlated bias and improve accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chenchen Kuai', 'Jiwan Jiang', 'Zihao Zhu', 'Hao Wang', 'Keshu Wu', 'Zihao Li', 'Yunlong Zhang', 'Chenxi Liu', 'Zhengzhong Tu', 'Zhiwen Fan', 'Yang Zhou']
  • Tags: ['ensemble-safety', 'model-auditing', 'behavioral-entanglement', 'LLM-evaluation', 'information-theoretic-metrics']

item.title: AtomEval: Atomic Evaluation of Adversarial Claims in Fact Verification
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AtomEval, an evaluation framework for fact verification under adversarial claim rewriting.
  • Decomposes claims into subject-relation-object-modifier (SROM) atoms and uses Atomic Validity Scoring (AVS) to judge truth-conditional consistency.
  • Shows standard metrics can mislabel semantically corrupted rewrites as successful and that validity-aware scoring yields more reliable signals.
  • Uses the framework to analyze and compare effectiveness of LLM-based adversarial generators.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hongyi Cen', 'Mingxin Wang', 'Yule Liu', 'Jingyi Zheng', 'Hanze Jia', 'Tan Tang', 'Yingcai Wu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial evaluation', 'fact verification', 'adversarial claim rewriting', 'truth-conditional consistency', 'LLM-based attacks']

item.title: An Empirical Analysis of Static Analysis Methods for Detection and Mitigation of Code Library Hallucinations
item.description:
Summary

  • Evaluates static analysis tools for detecting and mitigating code library hallucinations in LLM-generated code.
  • Finds static analysis can detect 16–70% of errors and 14–85% of library hallucinations, depending on model and dataset.
  • Provides an empirical upper bound on catchable cases (48.5%–77%) based on manual analysis of failures.
  • Concludes static analysis is a cost-effective mitigation for some hallucination errors but cannot fully prevent them.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Clarissa Miranda-Pena', 'Andrew Reeson', "C\\'ecile Paris", 'Josiah Poon', 'Jonathan K. Kummerfeld']
  • Tags: ['LLM code hallucinations', 'static analysis', 'input validation', 'attack detection/mitigation', 'robustness evaluation']

item.title: Beyond Social Pressure: Benchmarking Epistemic Attack in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces PPT-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for “epistemic attack” on LLMs via prompts that challenge knowledge, values, or identity.
  • Defines a Philosophical Pressure Taxonomy with four pressure types: Epistemic Destabilization, Value Nullification, Authority Inversion, Identity Dissolution; evaluates at L0 (baseline), L1 (single-turn), and L2 (multi-turn Socratic escalation).
  • Measures inconsistency and conversational capitulation across models, showing attacks reveal weaknesses beyond prior social-pressure/sycophancy benchmarks.
  • Tests multiple mitigation interventions and finds effectiveness varies by pressure type and model, including anchoring/persona-stability and contrastive decoding for open models.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking (Research)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Steven Au', 'Sujit Noronha']
  • Tags: ['epistemic attack', 'LLM robustness/mitigation', 'benchmarking', 'prompt-based security evaluation', 'sycophancy/mental-model manipulation']

item.title: Corruption-robust Offline Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning From Human Feedback
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robustness to adversarially corrupted offline datasets for multi-agent reinforcement learning from human feedback (MARLHF).
  • Analyzes performance degradation in game-theoretic terms (Nash equilibrium gap / coarse correlated equilibrium gap) under an epsilon-fraction strong-contamination model.
  • Proposes robust estimation and algorithmic solutions under uniform vs unilateral coverage assumptions.
  • Introduces intractability-reducing relaxation to CCE and provides quasi-polynomial-time guarantees with O(√ε) scaling.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Andi Nika', 'Debmalya Mandal', 'Parameswaran Kamalaruban', 'Adish Singla', "Goran Radanovi\\'c"]
  • Tags: ['data-corruption-robustness', 'offline-RL', 'MARLHF', 'adversarial-robustness', 'game-theoretic-equilibrium']

item.title: ALPINE: Closed-Loop Adaptive Privacy Budget Allocation for Mobile Edge Crowdsensing
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ALPINE, a closed-loop framework for adaptive privacy budget allocation in mobile edge crowdsensing (MECS).
  • Uses risk perception (channel/semantic/contextual/resource) to select a differential privacy budget via an offline-trained TD3 policy.
  • Applies local differential privacy perturbation before transmission and uses edge-side privacy-utility evaluation for feedback and policy refinement.
  • Evaluates against privacy attacks including membership inference, property inference, and reconstruction, showing improved privacy-utility trade-offs and reduced attack effectiveness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Guanjie Cheng', 'Siyang Liu', 'Xinkui Zhao', 'Yishan Chen', 'Junqin Huang', 'Linghe Kong', 'Shiguang Deng']
  • Tags: ['privacy-preserving machine learning', 'differential privacy', 'privacy risk adaptation', 'membership inference', 'reconstruction attacks']

item.title: DiffGradCAM: A Class Activation Map Using the Full Model Decision to Solve Unaddressed Adversarial Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DiffGradCAM and DiffGradCAM++ to generate class activation maps using the full model decision (logit differences) to address adversarial manipulation of saliency outputs.
  • Claims the method mitigates “passive fooling” where CAMs can be manipulated to be misleading without changing the model’s decision performance.
  • Introduces Salience-Hoax Activation Maps (SHAMs), an entropy-aware passive-fooling benchmark to evaluate CAM robustness under adversarial conditions.
  • Validates on multi-class tasks, comparing with standard GradCAM/GradCAM++ in non-adversarial and adversarial settings.

Paper Type

  • Research/Method (with benchmark and experiments)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jacob Piland', 'Chris Sweet', 'Adam Czajka']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'saliency/interpretability robustness', 'class activation maps', 'passive fooling', 'attack benchmark']

item.title: On the Robustness of Tabular Foundation Models: Test-Time Attacks and In-Context Defenses
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies adversarial vulnerabilities of tabular foundation models (TabPFN/TabICL), showing targeted test-time perturbations can significantly degrade accuracy.
  • Demonstrates misuse: tabular FM can generate transferable evasion examples that attack conventional models (random forests, XGBoost) and to a lesser extent deep tabular models.
  • Proposes defenses via robustification: adversarial fine-tuning (weight optimization) and an adversarial in-context training strategy that swaps in adversarially perturbed context without weight updates.
  • Frames tabular FM as both an adversarial target and a potential source of adversarial threats, emphasizing the need for robust evaluation and training.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mohamed Djilani', 'Thibault Simonetto', 'Karim Tit', 'Florian Tambon', 'Salah Ghamizi', 'Maxime Cordy', 'Mike Papadakis']
  • Tags: ['test-time attacks', 'adversarial examples', 'transferable evasion', 'in-context learning defenses', 'tabular foundation models']

item.title: AdaProb: Efficient Machine Unlearning via Adaptive Probability
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AdaProb, an efficient machine unlearning method that replaces final-layer output probabilities with pseudo-probabilities for target data to be forgotten.
  • Optimizes pseudo-probabilities to maximize forgetting while aligning with the model’s overall output distribution to reduce membership inference risk.
  • Updates model weights to achieve privacy-preserving unlearning with substantially lower computational cost than prior methods.
  • Empirically reports improved forgetting error (over 20%), better resistance to membership inference attacks, and reduced runtime (less than 50% of baseline methods).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zihao Zhao', 'Yuchen Yang', 'Anjalie Field', 'Yinzhi Cao']
  • Tags: ['machine unlearning', 'privacy attacks (membership inference)', 'training data removal', 'defense/mitigation']

item.title: LipKernel: Lipschitz-Bounded Convolutional Neural Networks via Dissipative Layers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes LipKernel, a CNN parameterization that enforces layer-wise Lipschitz bounds via linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) tied to dissipativity/supply rates.
  • Uses a 2-D Roesser-type state space model to parameterize dissipative convolution kernels, yielding standard-form layers evaluable without extra computational overhead.
  • Reports experiments showing faster runtime than prior Lipschitz-bounded CNN methods (e.g., Fourier-domain spectral parameterizations).
  • Targets robustness guarantees for learning-based perception/control systems (implicitly relevant to adversarial robustness).

Paper Type

item.title: IatroBench: Pre-Registered Evidence of Iatrogenic Harm from AI Safety Measures
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces IatroBench, a pre-registered evaluation benchmark for measuring iatrogenic harm caused by AI safety measures in clinical guidance.
  • Compares model outputs across physician vs. layperson framing for multiple frontier LLMs, focusing on omission harm (withholding needed/appropriate guidance) and commission harm (unsafe/incorrect guidance).
  • Finds identity-contingent withholding: safety-colliding action hit rates decrease in layperson framing, but clinically appropriate guidance is also omitted for physician framing, especially in heavily safety-trained models.
  • Identifies distinct failure modes including trained withholding, incompetence, and indiscriminate content filtering that disproportionately removes physician-like answers.

item.title: Preference Redirection via Attention Concentration: An Attack on Computer Use Agents
item.description:

  • Unlike prior work that targets VLM outputs directly, PRAC targets internal attention/preference mechanisms, making it potentially harder to detect.

item.title: Broken by Default: A Formal Verification Study of Security Vulnerabilities in AI-Generated Code
item.description:

  • Finds that 55.8% of artifacts contain at least one verified vulnerability; 1,055 are formally proven with satisfiability witnesses.
  • Shows limited impact from explicit security instructions, low coverage by existing industry tools (missing 97.8% of Z3-proven findings), and that self-review reduces detection but does not prevent generation.
  • Confirms several representative verified findings with runtime crashes using GCC AddressSanitizer.

item.title: AdaProb: Efficient Machine Unlearning via Adaptive Probability

  • Extends results to discrete settings, multi-turn interactions, stochastic defenses, and capacity-parity cases, while noting training-time alignment/architectural changes may still work.
